requirements.quote:
*  Receiving a HEADERS frame causes the stream to transition to
         "half-closed (local)".
requirements.condition: A HEADERS frame is received on the stream in the state described immediately before this chunk.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "half-closed (local)".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can receive HEADERS in the applicable state and inspect the resulting stream state.

requirements.quote:
*  Either endpoint can send a RST_STREAM frame to cause the stream
         to become "closed".  This releases the stream reservation.
requirements.condition: Either endpoint sends RST_STREAM on the reserved stream described by this state.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed" and release its reservation.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting stream state and reservation release are observable after RST_STREAM is sent.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send any type of frame other than RST_STREAM,
      WINDOW_UPDATE, or PRIORITY in this state.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame while the stream is in this state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending any frame type other than RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, or PRIORITY.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frame types can be checked against the three-member allowlist while the stream is in this state.

requirements.quote:
Receiving any type of frame other than HEADERS, RST_STREAM, or
      PRIORITY on a stream in this state MUST be treated as a connection
      error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: A frame other than HEADERS, RST_STREAM, or PRIORITY is received on a stream in this state.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject each disallowed frame type and verify the connection-level error code.

requirements.quote:
open:  A stream in the "open" state may be used by both peers to send
      frames of any type.  In this state, sending peers observe
      advertised stream-level flow-control limits (Section 5.2).
requirements.condition: A peer sends frames on an open stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Observe the advertised stream-level flow-control limits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exceeding the advertised stream-level flow-control limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Sent flow-controlled data can be measured against the advertised per-stream limit.

requirements.quote:
From this state, either endpoint can send a frame with an
      END_STREAM flag set, which causes the stream to transition into
      one of the "half-closed" states.  An endpoint sending an
      END_STREAM flag causes the stream state to become "half-closed
      (local)"; an endpoint receiving an END_STREAM flag causes the
      stream state to become "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.condition: An endpoint in the open state sends a frame with END_STREAM set.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "half-closed (local)" for the sending endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: The local stream state is observable after sending an END_STREAM frame.

requirements.quote:
From this state, either endpoint can send a frame with an
      END_STREAM flag set, which causes the stream to transition into
      one of the "half-closed" states.  An endpoint sending an
      END_STREAM flag causes the stream state to become "half-closed
      (local)"; an endpoint receiving an END_STREAM flag causes the
      stream state to become "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.condition: An endpoint in the open state receives a frame with END_STREAM set.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "half-closed (remote)" for the receiving endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: The local stream state is observable after receiving an END_STREAM frame.

requirements.quote:
Either endpoint can send a RST_STREAM frame from this state,
      causing it to transition immediately to "closed".
requirements.condition: Either endpoint sends RST_STREAM on an open stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected immediately after RST_STREAM is sent.

requirements.quote:
half-closed (local):  A stream that is in the "half-closed (local)"
      state cannot be used for sending frames other than WINDOW_UPDATE,
      PRIORITY, and RST_STREAM.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame on a stream in "half-closed (local)".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending any frame type other than WINDOW_UPDATE, PRIORITY, or RST_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frame types can be checked against the stated allowlist in this state.

requirements.quote:
A stream transitions from this state to "closed" when a frame is
      received with the END_STREAM flag set or when either peer sends a
      RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: A frame with END_STREAM set is received on a stream in "half-closed (local)".
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected after receiving the flagged frame.

requirements.quote:
A stream transitions from this state to "closed" when a frame is
      received with the END_STREAM flag set or when either peer sends a
      RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: Either peer sends RST_STREAM for a stream in "half-closed (local)".
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected after either locally sending or remotely receiving RST_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint can receive any type of frame in this state.
      Providing flow-control credit using WINDOW_UPDATE frames is
      necessary to continue receiving flow-controlled frames.  In this
      state, a receiver can ignore WINDOW_UPDATE frames, which might
      arrive for a short period after a frame with the END_STREAM flag
      set is sent.
requirements.condition: An endpoint wants to continue receiving flow-controlled frames on a stream in "half-closed (local)".
requirements.required_behavior: Provide flow-control credit using WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A flow-control test can verify that continued receipt is enabled only by providing WINDOW_UPDATE credit.

requirements.quote:
If an endpoint receives additional frames, other than
      WINDOW_UPDATE, PRIORITY, or RST_STREAM, for a stream that is in
      this state, it MUST respond with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of
      type STREAM_CLOSED.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives an additional frame other than WINDOW_UPDATE, PRIORITY, or RST_STREAM on a stream in "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a stream error of type STREAM_CLOSED.
requirements.why_checkable: Each disallowed inbound frame can be injected and the stream-scoped error code verified.

requirements.quote:
A stream that is "half-closed (remote)" can be used by the
      endpoint to send frames of any type.  In this state, the endpoint
      continues to observe advertised stream-level flow-control limits
      (Section 5.2).
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends frames on a stream in "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.required_behavior: Continue to observe advertised stream-level flow-control limits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exceeding the advertised stream-level flow-control limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Sent flow-controlled data can be measured against the advertised per-stream limit in this state.

requirements.quote:
A stream can transition from this state to "closed" by sending a
      frame with the END_STREAM flag set or when either peer sends a
      RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: The endpoint sends a frame with END_STREAM set on a stream in "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected after the endpoint sends the flagged frame.

requirements.quote:
A stream can transition from this state to "closed" by sending a
      frame with the END_STREAM flag set or when either peer sends a
      RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: Either peer sends RST_STREAM for a stream in "half-closed (remote)".
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state can be inspected after either locally sending or remotely receiving RST_STREAM.

requirements.quote: closed:  The "closed" state is the terminal state.
requirements.condition: A stream has entered the "closed" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the stream in the terminal "closed" state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transitioning the stream from "closed" to a non-closed state.
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent events can be applied and the implementation checked for an impermissible state transition.

requirements.quote:
A stream enters the "closed" state after an endpoint both sends
      and receives a frame with an END_STREAM flag set.  A stream also
      enters the "closed" state after an endpoint either sends or
      receives a RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has both sent and received a frame with END_STREAM set on the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: A test can perform both directional END_STREAM events and inspect the resulting state.

requirements.quote:
A stream enters the "closed" state after an endpoint both sends
      and receives a frame with an END_STREAM flag set.  A stream also
      enters the "closed" state after an endpoint either sends or
      receives a RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: An endpoint either sends or receives RST_STREAM for the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to "closed".
requirements.why_checkable: Both send and receive paths can be tested and the resulting stream state inspected.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send frames other than PRIORITY on a closed
      stream.  An endpoint MAY treat receipt of any other type of frame
      on a closed stream as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      STREAM_CLOSED, except as noted below.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame on a closed stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending any frame other than PRIORITY.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frames on closed streams can be checked to ensure only PRIORITY is emitted.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT send frames other than PRIORITY on a closed
      stream.  An endpoint MAY treat receipt of any other type of frame
      on a closed stream as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      STREAM_CLOSED, except as noted below.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a frame other than PRIORITY on a closed stream and none of the exceptions noted below applies.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat the receipt as a connection error of type STREAM_CLOSED.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a non-PRIORITY frame outside the exceptions and accept either the specified optional error handling or continued processing.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that sends a RST_STREAM frame on a stream that is in
      the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state could receive any type
      of frame.  The peer might have sent or enqueued for sending these
      frames before processing the RST_STREAM frame.  An endpoint MUST
      minimally process and then discard any frames it receives in this
      state.  This means updating header compression state for HEADERS
      and PUSH_PROMISE frames.  Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame also
      causes the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)", even
      when the PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on a closed stream.
      Additionally, the content of DATA frames counts toward the
      connection flow-control window.
requirements.condition: After sending RST_STREAM on a stream that was "open" or "half-closed (local)", the endpoint receives a frame on that now-closed stream before the peer processes the reset.
requirements.required_behavior: Minimally process the frame and then discard it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the received frame normally after minimal processing instead of discarding it.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can race inbound frames with RST_STREAM and observe required side effects while verifying that frame content is otherwise discarded.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that sends a RST_STREAM frame on a stream that is in
      the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state could receive any type
      of frame.  The peer might have sent or enqueued for sending these
      frames before processing the RST_STREAM frame.  An endpoint MUST
      minimally process and then discard any frames it receives in this
      state.  This means updating header compression state for HEADERS
      and PUSH_PROMISE frames.  Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame also
      causes the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)", even
      when the PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on a closed stream.
      Additionally, the content of DATA frames counts toward the
      connection flow-control window.
requirements.condition: A HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE frame is minimally processed after being received in the post-RST_STREAM closed state described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Update header compression state before discarding the frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discarding the frame without updating header compression state.
requirements.why_checkable: The compression context can be exercised by subsequent header blocks to detect whether it remained synchronized.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that sends a RST_STREAM frame on a stream that is in
      the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state could receive any type
      of frame.  The peer might have sent or enqueued for sending these
      frames before processing the RST_STREAM frame.  An endpoint MUST
      minimally process and then discard any frames it receives in this
      state.  This means updating header compression state for HEADERS
      and PUSH_PROMISE frames.  Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame also
      causes the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)", even
      when the PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on a closed stream.
      Additionally, the content of DATA frames counts toward the
      connection flow-control window.
requirements.condition: A PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on the closed stream in the post-RST_STREAM situation described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Cause the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)" before discarding the frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised stream's state can be inspected after the PUSH_PROMISE is minimally processed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that sends a RST_STREAM frame on a stream that is in
      the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state could receive any type
      of frame.  The peer might have sent or enqueued for sending these
      frames before processing the RST_STREAM frame.  An endpoint MUST
      minimally process and then discard any frames it receives in this
      state.  This means updating header compression state for HEADERS
      and PUSH_PROMISE frames.  Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame also
      causes the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)", even
      when the PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on a closed stream.
      Additionally, the content of DATA frames counts toward the
      connection flow-control window.
requirements.condition: A DATA frame is received on the closed stream in the post-RST_STREAM situation described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Count the DATA frame content toward the connection flow-control window before discarding the frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discarding the DATA content without charging it to connection-level flow control.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-level flow-control accounting can be inspected after the DATA frame is minimally processed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint can perform this minimal processing for all streams
      that are in the "closed" state.  Endpoints MAY use other signals
      to detect that a peer has received the frames that caused the
      stream to enter the "closed" state and treat receipt of any frame
      other than PRIORITY as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Endpoints can use frames that indicate that the
      peer has received the closing signal to drive this.  Endpoints
      SHOULD NOT use timers for this purpose.  For example, an endpoint
      that sends a SETTINGS frame after closing a stream can safely
      treat receipt of a DATA frame on that stream as an error after
      receiving an acknowledgment of the settings.  Other things that
      might be used are PING frames, receiving data on streams that were
      created after closing the stream, or responses to requests created
      after closing the stream.
requirements.condition: The endpoint has used a signal to detect that the peer received the frame that closed the stream, and it then receives a frame other than PRIORITY on that stream.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat the receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish peer receipt of the closing signal, inject a non-PRIORITY frame, and verify the optional connection error behavior.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint can perform this minimal processing for all streams
      that are in the "closed" state.  Endpoints MAY use other signals
      to detect that a peer has received the frames that caused the
      stream to enter the "closed" state and treat receipt of any frame
      other than PRIORITY as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Endpoints can use frames that indicate that the
      peer has received the closing signal to drive this.  Endpoints
      SHOULD NOT use timers for this purpose.  For example, an endpoint
      that sends a SETTINGS frame after closing a stream can safely
      treat receipt of a DATA frame on that stream as an error after
      receiving an acknowledgment of the settings.  Other things that
      might be used are PING frames, receiving data on streams that were
      created after closing the stream, or responses to requests created
      after closing the stream.
requirements.condition: An endpoint determines when the peer has received the frame that caused a stream to enter "closed".
requirements.required_behavior: Use non-timer signals for this detection when practicable.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation configuration and runtime behavior can be inspected for timer-based detection of peer receipt.

requirements.quote:
In the absence of more specific rules, implementations SHOULD treat
   the receipt of a frame that is not expressly permitted in the
   description of a state as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that PRIORITY can be sent and received in any
   stream state.
requirements.condition: No more specific rule applies and a frame not expressly permitted by the current state description is received.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A state/frame matrix can inject unspecified disallowed frames and verify the connection-level error code.

requirements.quote:
In the absence of more specific rules, implementations SHOULD treat
   the receipt of a frame that is not expressly permitted in the
   description of a state as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that PRIORITY can be sent and received in any
   stream state.
requirements.condition: A PRIORITY frame is sent or received in any stream state.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the PRIORITY frame in every stream state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Rejecting PRIORITY solely because of the stream state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send and receive PRIORITY in each stream state and verify state-based acceptance.

requirements.quote:
The rules in this section only apply to frames defined in this
   document.  Receipt of frames for which the semantics are unknown
   cannot be treated as an error, as the conditions for sending and
   receiving those frames are also unknown; see Section 5.5.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a frame whose semantics are unknown.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow the unknown frame to be handled without a state-rule error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating receipt of the unknown frame as an error based on the stream-state rules in this section.
requirements.why_checkable: An unknown extension frame can be injected in each state and the endpoint checked for improper error generation.
